questionText: How does the embedded server lifecycle relate to the Spring ApplicationContext?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can connect server creation and shutdown to the web ApplicationContext, distinguish server initialization from application readiness, and configure bounded graceful shutdown.
outOfScope: Treating server initialized as complete readiness
Claiming graceful shutdown is the Boot 3.3.1 default

claims.statement: A Spring Boot web ApplicationContext creates and manages an embedded WebServer through a WebServerFactory.
ServletWebServerInitializedEvent is published after the server is ready, while ApplicationReadyEvent occurs later after application and command-line runners.
Spring Boot 3.3.1 defaults server.shutdown to immediate; graceful shutdown is enabled explicitly and bounded by spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase.

examples.title: Listeners for servlet-server initialized and application-ready events

validation.command: Review the focused example against Java 17 and Spring Boot 3.3.1 APIs and configuration metadata
validation.expected: Both Boot 3.3 event types and getWebServer().getPort() usage are correct for a servlet application

examples.title: Random port and bounded graceful shutdown properties

validation.command: Focused embedded-server example gate parses the port, shutdown mode, and duration
validation.expected: Port zero, graceful mode, and 20-second phase timeout are valid Boot 3.3.1 properties

visuals.title: Context refresh, server event, runners, readiness, and shutdown flow

notes: The answer uses the Boot 3.3.1 immediate default rather than the changed default in newer Spring Boot lines.

review.notes: Lifecycle ownership, event order, readiness, and Boot 3.3.1 graceful-shutdown properties were checked against official Spring Boot documentation and API references. Java example remains manual review.
